fixes.explanation: You've got it, baker. The text says "As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue…" (Acts 17:2). A custom is just a habit, and Paul has one. Mine is checking the oven timer six times a minute, and it has never once made the cookies faster.

Not quite, baker. The text says "As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue…" (Acts 17:2). So the answer is True. A custom is a habit, like me peeking at the oven timer when I know it hasn't rung.
That's it, baker. Acts 17:2 says Paul "…reasoned with them from the Scriptures…" That's the Word of God on the table. And it goes on for three Sabbaths.
Different country, baker, but a good try. Acts 17:4 says "…a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women." Egyptians aren't mentioned anywhere in this passage.

That's right, baker. Acts 17:5 says they "…brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar." Notice the jealousy comes first. Then the troublemakers show up.

A debate would've been tidy, baker, but that's not what the text says happens. Acts 17:5 says they "…brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar." What we get is a mob and an uproar.

Not this time, baker. Acts 17:5 says they raided Jason's house in search of Paul and Silas, and verse 6 says "…when they could not find them…" So the mob doesn't find them there. The statement is False.

Yes, baker. They shout that all these men are "…defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!" (Acts 17:7). Caesar is the Roman emperor, so that's the charge they pick. The mob says it right after saying Jason welcomed them into his home.

Right, baker. Acts 17:9 says "…they collected bond from Jason and the others and then released them." Jason is the one the mob said had welcomed Paul and Silas into his home. He and the others walk out once the bond is collected.

You got it, baker. Acts 17:10 says that on arriving in Berea, "…they went into the Jewish synagogue." That's the same move as in Thessalonica. And verse 11 says the Bereans received the message with great eagerness.

Yes, baker. Acts 17:12 says "…many of them believed…" That comes right after verse 11, where the Bereans "examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true." They looked into it, and plenty of them came to believe.
Right, baker. Acts 17:12 says many believed "…along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men." The verse names both the women and the men. It's a big, mixed crowd of people who believed.
Not this time, baker. Acts 17:14 says "…Silas and Timothy remained in Berea." Timothy travels with Paul too (Acts 16:1-3). So the statement is False, because they stayed behind.
Yes, baker, False. Acts 17:14 says "…Silas and Timothy remained in Berea." Timothy travels with Paul too (Acts 16:1-3). He and Silas stay put while Paul goes on.
A fair guess, since Paul does go to Corinth later (Acts 18:1), but it's not the city here. Acts 17:15 says the escorts "…brought him to Athens…" Athens is the answer.

Yes, baker. The escorts return with "…instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible." (Acts 17:15). Paul is in Athens, since that's where the escorts brought him. So the word to Silas and Timothy is to hurry.
